imagePrompts.prompt: A patriotic Ghanaian classroom scene. The room is decorated with Ghana flags and a map. Children are dressed in traditional wear and school uniforms, waving small flags. The atmosphere is festive and proud.
Children celebrating Ghana's history. A group is looking at a large colorful map of Ghana on the wall. Another group is marching like soldiers in a 'March Past'. The teacher smiles and claps.
A storytelling circle. The teacher is telling the story of Independence Day using puppets or pictures of the 'Big Six'. Children are listening intently and raising hands to ask questions.
Children standing near a large outline map of Ghana on the wall. They are holding colored paper cut-outs. One child pins a color to a region on the map. They are identifying home regions.
A child picking a colored paper that matches a region on the map. The teacher helps them locate their 'home region'. On tables, children are grouping cut-out papers by color and counting them.
Community circle time using the 'Pass the Ball' game. A child holds a ball and shares a story about a festival or Independence Day. A poster of the 6th March celebration is visible.

Children playing the 'Be the Word' game. Three children stand in a line, each holding a card with one word written on it. They stand apart to show spaces between words. The teacher points to the spaces.
Small groups arranging cut-up sentence strips on a table. They place a finger between word cards to create spaces. They look happy as they form a sentence. Simple literacy activity.
Interactive read aloud about Independence Day. The teacher holds a Big Book showing parade scenes. Children engage with the text and use pictures to understand new words.
Children drawing a scene of Independence Day celebrations with crayons. Some are using counters to do simple subtraction problems on the side. Integrated art and math.
Children standing at attention, some with hands on their chests, singing the national anthem. A collage of the Ghana flag made of fabric scraps is displayed on the wall.
Small groups of children working on a large Ghana flag collage. They are pasting red, yellow, and green pieces of material. One child adds the black star. Collaborative art project.
Children singing an alphabet song and pointing to letters on a wall chart. They perform actions for each letter. The classroom is bright and filled with print.
A literacy and numeracy mix. Children identifying a focus letter in a word on the board. They use counters to subtract the count of that letter from the total letters in the word.
Children dancing to Ghanaian music. They are moving rhythmically. Some play improvised instruments like shakers. The mood is energetic and cultural.
A 'Kiddies March Past' on the school field. Children marching in line to a beat. One child stands on a small box acting as the President, taking the salute. Playful patriotism.
Children working with bottle tops on a mat. They have a pile of 10 tops and are separating them into two smaller piles (e.g., 5 and 5, or 6 and 4). Learning decomposition.
A child looking at a card with 5 dots. They are drawing circles around subgroups of dots (e.g., circling 3 and 2) to show how the number 5 is made. Focused numeracy activity.
